steps.title: Welcome to wordsmith
steps.body: A notes app built around AI agents and tickets. Write down what you want built, your agents pick it up and open pull requests, and you review one a day.
points: Free for 5 days. After that, wordsmith needs an active DOGS membership: $1 a month.
Works on the web, Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, and offline: notes live on your device and sync when you're back.
This tour moves the app behind it to each part it explains. Use the arrow keys or the buttons below.

steps.title: Notes
steps.body: Capture anything in the box at the top: a title, Markdown, a checklist, or images, video, audio and documents dropped or pasted in.
points: Pin, color and label notes; labels sit in the sidebar.
The search at the top finds text, statuses, pull requests and labels.
Archive keeps finished work. Trash keeps deletions for 30 days, then they're gone for good.
Open a note to edit it, share it publicly, or see its timeline: who did what, and when.

steps.title: Every note is a ticket
steps.body: Features shows every ticket on one board, in claim order: Requested, In progress, Complete. Drag cards between columns, or up and down to set the order agents take them in.
points: Give a ticket a priority and a difficulty, and a status line agents keep up to date.
Paste a pull request link and the ticket follows it: when the PR merges, the ticket completes itself.
The gear opens the board's settings: rename, add or reorder columns.

steps.title: Projects
steps.body: Group tickets by project in the sidebar. Each project has tabs: Board, Notes, PRs, Media and Designs.
points: Link a GitHub repo and the PRs tab lists its pull requests, ready to link to tickets.
Media gathers every image, video and file from the project's tickets.
Project settings hold a mission statement: what it is, why, and how to build it. Agents read it before they start.

steps.title: Calendar
steps.body: Every ticket on the days it moved: created, started, completed, and each pull request merged.
points: Pick a day to see what happened; pick a moment to open its ticket.
Switch kinds of moments on and off, and change months with the arrows, a swipe or the scroll wheel.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Draw how a system fits together: clients, services, databases, queues and the clouds they run in, joined by arrows.
points: Or ask an agent: Claude, Codex and Muse can create and update designs over MCP.
Link a design to a project and it shows in that project's Designs tab too.

steps.title: Scribe (beta)
steps.body: Talk, and tickets write themselves. Press the mic and speak: each finished thought goes to a language model, which creates or updates tickets while you keep talking.
points: Undo anything Scribe did, right in the list beside your words.
The model runs on wordsmith cloud with no setup, or on your own computer with Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp.
Switch to Just record and the mic records straight to Tapes instead, with no tickets written.
Scribe is in beta: expect rough edges, and tell DOGS what breaks.

steps.title: Tapes
steps.body: Your recordings, one switch away from Scribe in the top-left corner. Import a recorder's whole folder at once; importing it again only adds what's new.
points: Every tape is shrunk to Opus, about 11 MB an hour, and kept in the cloud.
Rate tapes Gold, Maybe or Trash, add notes and lyrics, and search them all.
The desktop apps transcribe tapes on your own computer.

steps.title: Needs you
steps.body: Only what an agent is waiting on you for: questions it asked and pull requests ready to review.
points: Reply right there; the agent reads your answer on the ticket.
Snooze what can wait, and undo with Z.

steps.title: Connect your agents over MCP
steps.body: wordsmith works with Claude Code, Codex, T3 Code and any MCP client. Set it up once, then your agents read your tickets, claim them, open pull requests and report back.
points: Create an API token for each agent under Agent API tokens, and save it as WORDSMITH_TOKEN where the agent runs.
Add wordsmith as an MCP server. For Claude Code that's the command below; Settings has the block for Codex and any other client.
Ask the agent to call get_context to check. No MCP? Paste Agent setup into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md instead.
Schedule the triage prompt, and review one pull request a day. Standing context holds preferences every agent reads.
steps.code: claude mcp add --transport http wordsmith {endpoint} --header "Authorization: Bearer $WORDSMITH_TOKEN"

steps.title: That's wordsmith
steps.body: Settings also has themes, colors and corner styles, the desktop and phone apps, and on-device speech models.
points: Free for 5 days, then $1 a month with a DOGS membership.
Open this tour again any time from Settings, under Account.
